title: Rasam
description: A thin, peppery tamarind-and-tomato broth tempered with mustard seeds and curry leaves — light, tangy, and often the last course of a South Indian meal, eaten with rice.

ingredients.name: Tamarind
ingredients.notes: a small lemon-sized ball, soaked and pulp extracted

steps: Pressure cook the toor dal with 1 cup of the water for 3-4 whistles until soft. Mash and set aside.
In a pot, combine the tamarind pulp, chopped tomatoes, remaining water, rasam powder, turmeric and salt. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until the tomatoes soften and the raw tamarind smell fades.
Add the mashed dal and crushed black pepper, and simmer for another 5 minutes — do not let it come to a rolling boil once the dal is added, or the rasam can turn frothy and lose its light texture.
For the tempering, heat ghee in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds, letting them splutter, then add the dried red chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida.
Pour the tempering over the rasam and garnish with coriander leaves. Serve hot with steamed rice.
